requirements.text: The SCE-MI infrastructure provides clock (and reset) generation and shared clock control using handshake signals with the transactor.
Any transactor can instruct the SCE-MI infrastructure to stop the controlled clock and thus cause controlled time to freeze.
All transactors are told by the SCE-MI infrastructure when the controlled clock is stopped.
Any transactor must function correctly if controlled time is stopped due to operations of another transactor, even if the transactor in question does not itself need to stop the clock.
All transactors are clocked by a free running uncontrolled clock that is provided by the SCE-MI hardware side infrastructure.

Define the security state of the DUT during a 'frozen' time state, ensuring that the SCE-MI infrastructure prevents unauthorized access or modification of the DUT's internal registers or memory while the clock is stopped.
Implement an authentication mechanism for the binding process between software models and hardware message ports to ensure only authorized software components can interact with the DUT.

Define the required state behavior for transactors during a clock-stop event, specifically whether they must maintain current state, enter a high-impedance state, or continue processing asynchronous logic.
Define the error reporting and recovery mechanism for the SCE-MI infrastructure when clock generation or synchronization signals fail.

Define specific latency budgets (e.g., 'The SCE-MI infrastructure shall deliver a message from a software port proxy to a hardware port macro in less than X microseconds') and throughput targets (e.g., 'The interface shall support a minimum sustained throughput of Y million transactions per second').
Specify the maximum supported scale, such as 'The infrastructure shall support at least 100 concurrent message channels and 50 independent clock domains without performance degradation.'

Define a maximum latency for the ServiceLoop execution (e.g., 'The ServiceLoop shall complete in under 50 microseconds when no messages are pending') and provide guidance on the required polling frequency to maintain real-time performance.
